proposal: The Mandate recommends that FERC limit its Natural Gas Act pipeline certificate decisions to whether there is a need for the gas and limit its NEPA analysis to the effects of the pipeline itself rather than upstream and downstream emissions. It also recommends that needed pipelines be reviewed and built in a timely manner and that Congress, the states and FERC consider better protection and compensation for property owners. The related point that FERC should not use climate change to stop LNG projects is tracked under c12-04.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-18 FERC has made pipeline approvals faster in procedure, but the Mandate's two specific standards (need-only certificate decisions and project-only NEPA review) were not found adopted in the Federal Register. On 2025-08-29 the Energy Secretary used section 403 of the DOE Organization Act to ask FERC to rescind its never-finalized 2022 draft certificate policy statement and keep the 1999 framework; FERC published the request on 2025-09-05 (90 FR 42963) for comment through 2025-09-09 and the notice states that action remains pending, with no outcome found. FERC issued a final rule on 2025-10-10 (90 FR 48221, effective 2025-11-10, confirmed 2026-02-24) removing 18 CFR 157.23, which barred construction authorization while rehearing was pending; it received 23 comments, 11 opposed and 12 in support, and the rule states that FERC continues to apply the existing Natural Gas Act standards and that the change affects only when construction may begin, not a project's environmental effects. On 2026-05-27 FERC proposed raising blanket certificate cost limits (91 FR 31371; prior-notice cap from 41.1 to 86 million dollars); comments closed 2026-07-27 and no final rule was found.

timeline.event: FERC seeks stakeholder input on whether and how to adjust the cost limits for pipeline projects built under blanket certificates without case-specific authorization.

The Energy Secretary asks FERC under section 403 of the DOE Organization Act to rescind the 2022 draft Updated Certificate Policy Statement, end the related proceeding and keep using the 1999 policy statement; FERC publishes the request for comment on 2025-09-05 with comments due 2025-09-09.

FERC publishes a final rule, effective 2025-11-10, removing 18 CFR 157.23, which had barred construction authorizations for certain approved gas facilities while rehearing was pending; FERC ties the change to reliability and resource adequacy concerns and received 23 comments (11 opposed, 12 in support).
FERC responds to rehearing arguments and confirms the effective date of the October 2025 final rule.

FERC proposes revisions to the blanket certificate program: higher cost limits (prior notice from 41.1 to 86 million dollars, automatic authorization from 14.5 to 30 million), annual adjustment by a different index, wider scope for compressor station and abandonment projects, and a two-year in-service deadline; comments closed 2026-07-27, with the pipeline trade group INGAA supporting higher limits and AGA, APGA, EDF and NGSA raising concerns about ratepayer impacts and oversight.

title: Narrow FERC gas pipeline review to market need and project-level NEPA; speed approvals
uncertainties: FERC's response to the Energy Secretary's request was not found in the Federal Register (the notice itself says action remains pending), so the draft statement may or may not have been rescinded; a web search on 2026-10-18 surfaced only law-firm posts and the notice. The blanket certificate proposal was read in full (about 116,000 characters, in two parts); it does not mention executive orders and does not adopt a NEPA scope standard, though it proposes removing compressor station expansions from a categorical exclusion. The 2026-02-24 confirmation rule was read as a Federal Register API record only (abstract and dates), not in full text. No Federal Register document addressed limiting NEPA review to a pipeline's own effects or greenhouse gas analysis in certificate cases. FERC orders on individual certificates and ferc.gov orders were not examined. Overlaps with c12-04, which covers DOE LNG export approvals and the FERC climate point.
